statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-120144 (PostgreSQL type-cache invalidation gap executes arbitrary code) affects only PostgreSQL 18: the PostgreSQL security page, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120144/, says versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected and lists 18.7 as the only fixed release. The flaw is in the type cache's in_progress_list mechanism, which deferred updates to the RelIdToTypeIdCacheHash table and could miss an invalidation for a composite type changed while its cache entry was being populated. That mechanism was added by commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/b85a9d046efdd27775cbe7db9e92aad96aab4ada ("Avoid looping over all type cache entries in TypeCacheRelCallback()"), which is in REL_18_BETA1 and not in REL_17_0, and the fix, commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/016b63271fb794436255ae13917793486a6c450f ("Replace typcache.c's buggy in_progress_list"), is tagged Security: CVE-2026-120144 and Backpatch-through: 18. At every PostgreSQL 16 release this owner publishes, REL_16_13 through REL_16_16, typcache.c has neither in_progress_list nor RelIdToTypeIdCacheHash; the 16.16 copy is https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_16_16/src/backend/utils/cache/typcache.c and the others match. The postgres server binary in every published DHI postgresql16 build for Alpine 3.23 (16.13-r0, 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0) reports its PostgreSQL 16 release on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index), and none of the patches applied by Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, touch typcache.c. The 16.16 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.16/, do not list this CVE. Alpine's postgresql16 16.16-r0 secfixes list CVE-2026-120144, but upstream's own advisory places PostgreSQL 16 outside the affected range.

PostgreSQL states that only major version 18 is affected by CVE-2026-120144 (PostgreSQL type-cache invalidation gap executes arbitrary code) and that versions before PostgreSQL 18 are unaffected: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120144/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120144. The 18.7 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.7/, describe the fix as replacing the type cache's in_progress_list mechanism. That mechanism is present in src/backend/utils/cache/typcache.c from REL_18_0 but absent from it at every PostgreSQL 17 release this owner publishes (REL_17_7 through REL_17_12; for example https://github.com/postgres/postgres/blob/REL_17_12/src/backend/utils/cache/typcache.c), and the 17.12 release notes do not list CVE-2026-120144. This owner publishes PostgreSQL 17 only: every published build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0) has a postgres server binary reporting that 17.x release on both x86_64 and aarch64, and none of the Alpine patches applied in the 17.12-r0 APKBUILD touch the type cache. Alpine's postgresql17 17.12-r0 secfixes list CVE-2026-120144 (https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD), but upstream does not consider major version 17 affected.

statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120144 (PostgreSQL type-cache invalidation gap executes arbitrary code) in 18.7 for major version 18: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120144/ lists 18.7 as the fixed release for 18, and the 18.7 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.7/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/2950cc7897a2c10f080f308dbef3b80665c6fd71 on the REL_18_STABLE branch, tagged Security: CVE-2026-120144 and Backpatch-through: 18, in the REL_18_7 release tag and not in REL_18_6. It changes only src/backend/utils/cache/typcache.c, removing the in_progress_list mechanism and instead keeping, and checking the validity of, entries in the relation-to-type hash table. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the files this fix changes, and it lists CVE-2026-120144 under its 18.7-r0 secfixes. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository (x86_64 and aarch64) publishes packages built from source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0. The vulnerable code is in the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres, which the postgresql18 package ships in every one of those builds on both architectures. We checked every published postgresql18 package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): the postgres server binary in 18.7-r0 reports PostgreSQL 18.7, while the earlier builds 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0 and 18.6-r0 report 18.1, 18.2, 18.3, 18.4 and 18.6. The fix adds no new message text, so the boundary rests on the release version that the server binary of each build reports. The earlier builds are upstream releases before 18.7, so they are affected; 18.7-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.
